# Tear Down AWS VPN

Tears the AWS VPN down: removes the router's AWS block (if any is there) under a revert timer after a Work Center approval, proves it gone, then - for a target deployed in AWS - plans the destroy, shows it on a second card and applies exactly that plan (PID S13 criterion 5, R2, ADR 0068).

*Generated by `itential/workflows/describe.py` from `itential/workflows/tear-down-aws-vpn.json`; a test keeps them equal, so a change goes into `build.py`, not this page. 184 tasks in 18 steps.*

## How it runs

- Through the Operations Manager automation "Tear Down AWS VPN": .
- From the endpoint trigger "Tear Down AWS VPN from the branded page" (route `tear-down-aws-vpn`).

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | The lab edge router whose AWS VPN to tear down |
| `change_note` | string | yes | Why, shown to the approver and written to the change request (may be empty) |

## Where it waits for a person

- `2c` approval: Approve removing the router's AWS block (step 10): the view `/work-center/task/InteractiveHTML`; no group set, so anyone who can open the task.
- `5f` approval: Approve destroying the AWS side (step 16): the view `/work-center/task/InteractiveHTML`; no group set, so anyone who can open the task.
- `cc4` Fix change request by hand (step 18): the view `/work-center/task/InteractiveHTML`; no group set, so anyone who can open the task.

## What it touches

- Gateway services: `config-push-revert` (2), `lab-edge` (3), `terraform-run` (4)
- Python on the Gateway runner: 13 tasks
- WorkCenter `InteractiveHTML` (3)
- lab-servicenow:1.0.0 `createStandardChange` (1)
- lab-servicenow:1.0.0 `updateStandardChange` (6)
- Work Center: 3 tasks
- Everything else is the Platform's own engine: queries, evaluations, strings, job variables.

## When it stops: what the job says

| Step | Task | What `error` says |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `9a0c` the inputs were refused | the inputs were refused before anything ran (see input_check for which input and why): nothing was sent to a device |
| 3 | `cef` the change request was not opened | ServiceNow did not open the change request, so nothing was planned, read or changed (fail closed); see change_texts |
| 8 | `b0` the plan could not run | the Gateway could not make Tear Down's plan (see teardown_plan / push_plan): nothing was sent to the router, nothing changed in AWS |
| 8 | `b1` why there is no plan | `stdout_json.message` of the job variable `teardown_plan` |
| 8 | `b2` the removal lines could not be made | lab-edge removal did not answer (see removal_result): nothing was sent to the router, nothing changed in AWS |
| 8 | `b3` why there is no push plan | `stdout_json.message` of the job variable `push_plan` |
| 8 | `b4` config-push-revert refuses it | config-push-revert's check refused the removal (see check_result): nothing was sent to the router, nothing changed in AWS |
| 8 | `b5` the router could not be read | lab-edge absent could not read the router before the card (see absent_before): nothing was sent to the router, nothing changed in AWS |
| 9 | `c83` ServiceNow refused Implement | ServiceNow did not move the change request to Implement after the approval (see change_number), so nothing was applied |
| 11 | `36` the approved removal could not start | the removal's parameters could not be read after the approval: nothing was sent to the router |
| 15 | `a7` the discard did not run | the rejected destroy plan could not be discarded; it stays in the state bucket until removed |
| 17 | `c0` the push could not finish | the Gateway could not run config-push-revert or read its answer (push_result): check the router - the removal may be live and unsaved, or pending until the revert timer rolls it back. Nothing changed in AWS |
| 17 | `c2` why the removal was not kept | `stdout_json.message` of task 3f's `result` |
| 17 | `c3` the proof could not run | lab-edge absent could not read the router after the removal step (absent_result; router_state says what was pushed): the AWS side was NOT touched - check the router, then Tear Down again |
| 17 | `c4` the block is not gone | lab-edge absent still finds part of the block after the removal step (absent_result.left; router_state says what was pushed): the AWS side was NOT touched |
| 17 | `c5` the destroy could not be planned | the router is clean; the Gateway could not plan the AWS destroy (destroy_plan_result): nothing changed in AWS - Tear Down again to remove it |
| 17 | `c6` the destroy did not complete | the router is clean; terraform apply of the destroy did not finish (apply_result): part of the AWS side may be left - check it, then Tear Down again |
| 17 | `c7` something is left | the destroy applied, but terraform-run outputs still reports outputs (outputs_result): check AWS |

## When it finishes: what the job says

| Step | Task | What `outcome` says |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | `4f` the outcome: router only | torn down: nothing of the router's AWS block is left (removed and saved, or none there - router_state says which - and proved gone); nothing of this target is deployed in AWS |
| 15 | `a1` the router rejection | rejected in Work Center: nothing was sent to the router and nothing changed in AWS |
| 15 | `a6` the AWS rejection | nothing of the router's AWS block is left (proved gone); the AWS destroy was rejected in Work Center, so the AWS side stays (about $1 a day) - Tear Down again to remove it |
| 16 | `66` the outcome: torn down | torn down: nothing of the router's AWS block is left (removed and saved, or none there - router_state says which - and proved gone), and the AWS side was destroyed - nothing of the deployment is left |
